subject: Serve mode scenarios and migration checklist
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@atlascare.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — hosting modes, migration scenarios, and checklist

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: we covered the demo of the Redwood runtime and ran a short throughput test with a sample clinical prompt. You flagged three constraints that will drive mode selection: PHI handling (HIPAA), predictable throughput for peak-hours, and minimizing migration effort from your current stack.

Summary of options (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to production, minimal ops, lower TCO for variable loads. Not recommended if PHI must remain in your VPC.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): predictable throughput, supports tenancy isolation, easy SLA upgrade. Good fit for predictable API traffic with controlled data flows.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control (KMS, private networking), required for strict PHI/regulatory needs; longer ramp and procurement time.

Migration scenarios we should qualify:
1) From a third-party LLM API (you mentioned MedPrompt/MedAPI): mostly router-level changes; we can replicate prompt templates and map model params. Accounting for rate limits and tokenization differences is usually trivial, but you should expect a 1–2 week validation window for regression checks.
2) From a self-hosted Triton/TensorRT cluster: requires model artifact conversion (we support standard checkpoints and can assist with conversions), KV cache transfer planning, and verifying inference kernels — 3–6 weeks typical depending on model size and tests.
3) From legacy GPU farms (custom gRPC endpoints): often the heaviest lift — we usually do a small adapter shim to replace the old endpoint then run a staged traffic migration. Plan for infra questions and network egress rules.

Action items / ask from you (can reply inline):
- Confirm whether PHI will be sent to the Redwood endpoint in any test or prod flow. (yes/no)
- Peak qps and 99th pct latency SLO target for inference (tokens/s or req/s).
- Which model family do you plan to run (open Llama variant, internal fine-tune, proprietary)?
- Procurement contact + timeline (procurement@atlascare.com listed?)
- Any regulatory artifacts we should plan to provide (SOC2, BAA/DPA draft, pen-test reports).

Attachments: I’ve included a short hosting comparison and a migration checklist to guide answers. If it helps, we can kick off a 2-week Dedicated PoC (reserved capacity) that mirrors your expected peak and run regression tests against a prompt suite.

Proposed next step: a 30-min follow-up to confirm the checklist and decide PoC vs light Hosted pilot. Link: https://calendar.redwood.com/rishi/30min

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — hosting modes, migration scenarios, and checklist

Thanks Rishi — solid recap. Quick answers and clarifications: 
- PHI: yes, production traffic will include PHI. We can run redacted test data during PoC but prod must be VPC/private.
- Peak: ~180 req/s at 95th percentile for our primary clinical triage API. Target 99th pct latency <= 250ms for single-turn prompts.
- Model family: currently using a finetuned LLaMA-2 variant (7B) and some experiments with a 13B internal model.
- Procurement: procurement@atlascare.com is correct; timeline is end of Q3 for baseline contract (we're pushing to have a decision by Sept 15).

Two ask items from our side: 
1) Can you provide a ballpark pricing for Dedicated capacity (2 reserved A100-equivalent nodes) vs Private VPC (same hardware footprint)? We need ranges for procurement.
2) If we go Private, what is the expected on-prem delivery window (assuming we manage hardware procurement)?

We also use MedPrompt as our current external API for non-PHI workloads — we'd like to avoid regressions in accuracy and latency when moving prompts over. Have you done migrations from MedPrompt before?

Appreciate the attachments. We'll review and get back with procurement contact.

— Alex

alex@atlascare.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — hosting modes, migration scenarios, and checklist

Alex — great, thanks for the quick answers. Short replies to your asks and an initial recommendation: 

Pricing (ballpark) — high level monthly ranges, assuming 24/7 footprint:
- Dedicated (2x A100-equivalent reserved): $28k–$40k/month depending on commitment term and quantization profile. Includes SLA, autoscaling buffer, and 90-day retention of request logs by default.
- Private VPC (managed control plane + customer VPC): $45k–$70k/month + integration onboarding fee (one-time). On-prem delivery (if you provide hardware) typically 4–8 weeks for image, networking, and KMS integration; full validation may push to 8–12 weeks.
- Hosted pilot (no PHI): $4k–$8k/month for light usage; quick ramp but not suitable for PHI.

Migration notes: 
- From MedPrompt: yes, we have migrated several customers from external APIs. Typical flow is a "router adapter" during cutover so you can A/B traffic for 1–2 weeks, with a prompt regression suite run in parallel. We handle tokenization diffs and provide small prompt-engineering tweaks when needed.
- From self-hosted Triton: we'll convert model artifacts and validate kernel paths; sometimes requires a small recompile step. Expect collaboration from your ML infra team.
- From legacy GPU farms: suggest an incremental approach — route a subset of traffic to Redwood Dedicated, verify metrics, then increase. We provide tracing hooks so you can compare outputs.

Security/regulatory: we will provide a DPA/BAA template and SOC2 type II report on request. For PHI the Private VPC path is the recommended option to meet your risk profile.

Proposed immediate next steps (pick one):
A) Private VPC discovery call (60m) — include your security lead and infra lead so we can scope VPC peering, KMS, and compliance artifacts.
B) Dedicated 2-week PoC using non-PHI test traffic (fast to stand up; can mirror your peak qps).
C) Hosted pilot for non-PHI endpoints + parallel plan for Private for PHI traffic.

I’ll loop in Procurement if you want us to provision an MSA/PO template. Also attaching the hosting comparison and a filled example of the migration checklist — see the comments column for typical values.

Would Friday 8/6 at 9:30am PT for the discovery call work?

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
